Title: Weighing Galaxy Clusters with Gas. I. On the Methods of Computing Hydrostatic Mass Bias
Authors: Erwin T. Lau, Daisuke Nagai, Kaylea Nelson
Year: 2013
Abstract: Mass estimates of galaxy clusters from X-ray and Sunyeav-Zel'dovich observations assume the intracluster gas is in hydrostatic equilibrium with their gravitational potential. In this work, we show that these two methods for computing the hydrostatic mass bias are equivalent by demonstrating that the equation used in the second method can be derived from taking spatial averages of the Euler equation. Specifically, we identify the correspondences of individual terms in these two methods mathematically and show that these correspondences are valid to within a few percent level using hydrodynamical simulations of galaxy cluster formation. In addition, we compute the mass bias associated with the acceleration of gas and show that its contribution is small in the virialized regions in the interior of galaxy cluster, but becomes non-negligible in the cluster outskirts of massive clusters where materials are being actively accreted. We discuss implications for understanding the origin of hydrostatic mass biases and for characterizing them using hydrodynamical simulations as well as observations.

args.claim: Nelson, Lau & Nagai 2014 (arXiv:1404.4636) give a redshift-universal non-thermal pressure fraction f_nth(r) = P_rand/P_tot = 1 - A{1 + exp[-((r/r200m)/B)^gamma]} with A = 0.452 +/- 0.001, B = 0.841 +/- 0.008, gamma = 1.628 +/- 0.019. The fit is accurate to about 10% over 0.1 <= r/r200m <= 1.5 and out to z = 1.5. It gives about 10% in the core rising to about 50% near r200m; there is no systematic mass dependence for M200m >= 6e14 Msun/h, and rapidly accreting clusters are 5-15% higher. The thermal-only HSE mass is corrected as M_tot = M_HSE,th + extra term from d(f_nth P_tot)/dr, i.e. P_tot = P_th/(1-f_nth). This is ready for d-01/d-04.
args.note: Formula Eq. 7 of 1404.4636. In the r200c scaling, P_rand/P_tot reaches about 45% at r200c at z=1.5, twice the z=0 value. So r200m is the radius to use.

args.claim: Benchmark table (verified quotes in references.bib). (1) FLAMINGO (2409.07849): median b_HSE = (M_HSE-M500c)/M500c of about -0.1 for groups and -0.2 for clusters; the scatter is smallest, about 0.1, at M500c ~ 1e14 Msun; at fixed true mass M_HSE rises with z for groups and falls for clusters, and the scatter grows; the bias is insensitive to the analytic profile form but sensitive to goodness of fit, and it depends on feedback. (2) X-COP (1805.00034): median f_nth about 6% at R500 and about 10% at R200; 1-b = 0.85 +/- 0.05 for Planck SZ masses; the B about 0.6 needed by CMB plus counts is excluded. (3) Wicker+22 (2204.12823): 3.8 sigma evidence for z-dependence of B with a Planck Omega_m prior; the result is sample-dependent and degenerate with Omega_m; B about 0.8. (4) SPT (1404.6250): clusters at 0.6<z<1.2 are about 40% cooler in the inner (r<0.1R500) and outer (r>R500) scaled temperature than clusters at 0.3<z<0.6; minimal pressure evolution outside the core. (5) Lau+13 (1306.3993): the summation and averaging (Euler/Jeans) bias methods are equivalent; the acceleration term is small inside but non-negligible in the outskirts of massive accreting clusters.
args.note: Quotes validated for 1404.4636, 2409.07849, 1805.00034, 2204.12823, 1404.6250 and 1306.3993. Most values come from abstracts read through get_arxiv_metadata. No figures were extracted.

args.claim: The HACC CGD and CTP emulators output scaled profiles, rho_gas/rho_crit(z) and T/T500, on 19 log-spaced bins in r/R500c from 0.0154 to 2.74. Both are trained only for z = 0 to 0.4987, so z=1 is unavailable and the high redshift used is z=0.4987. The halo mass bin and the T500 convention are not reported by the tool.
args.note: Answers q-01 and q-02. Fiducial values are the centre of the design: kappa_w=3, e_w=0.6, M_seed=1.3, v_kin=0.65, eps_kin=0.61, omega_m=0.1375, sigma_8=0.8. Because the profiles are already scaled, a self-similar rescaling of z=0 to z=0.4987 leaves the scaled profiles unchanged. Any difference between the two redshifts is therefore shape evolution only.

args.claim: Finite-difference log slopes in ln-space (grid spacing 0.2878). At z=0: dln rho/dln r = -1.86, -2.54, -2.93 and dln T/dln r = -0.27, -0.58, -0.91 at r/R500 = 0.49, 1.0, 1.54. At z=0.4987: dln rho/dln r = -1.87, -2.74, -3.10 and dln T/dln r = -0.35, -0.51, -1.07. The 1-sigma uncertainty at R500 is about 0.10-0.16 on the density slope and 0.05-0.14 on the temperature slope.
args.note: Slopes at 0.49 and 1.54 use central differences across neighbouring bins. The slope at R500 uses the bracketing bins 0.866 and 1.155, whose geometric midpoint is exactly 1.0. R200c is assumed to be about 1.5 R500c (NFW with c of about 4) and is taken at the 1.54 bin. Errors are computed by treating the GP std of adjacent bins as independent, which is conservative. The rho_gas slope is used as the n slope (constant mu).

args.claim: The HSE mass is M_HSE(<x R500)/M500 = -(x t/2)(s_n + s_T), assuming kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500) and mu=0.59. With this, M_HSE/M500 = 0.41, 0.93+-0.05, 1.27 at z=0 and 0.38, 0.84+-0.05, 1.22 at z=0.4987, at r/R500 = 0.49, 1.0, 1.54. The implied b_HSE,500c is 0.075 at z=0 and 0.16 at z=0.4987. The convention-independent shape-only shift in M_HSE,500c from z=0 to z=0.4987 is -9.2% +- about 8%.
args.note: The absolute b_HSE depends on the assumed T500 normalisation, which the emulator does not document. The ratio between redshifts depends only on self-similar T500 scaling at fixed M500. The shift decomposes as follows. Scaled T at R500 falls from 0.592 to 0.518, a factor of 0.876, or -12.4%. The slope sum steepens from -3.13 to -3.24, a factor of 1.037, or +3.7%. Lower scaled outer temperature at higher z drives the drop. Its sign matches FLAMINGO's falling HSE mass with z for clusters (q-05). The significance is only about 1.2 sigma under conservative independent-bin errors.

args.claim: Comparison plots of the emulated profiles at z=0 and z=0.4987 (fiducial parameters) are in Figure 6 (CGD) and Figure 7 (CTP). Scaled density agrees within about 2% over 0.2-0.9 R500 but is about 13% lower at 1.5 R500 at z=0.4987. Scaled temperature is lower at z=0.4987 at all radii above 0.03 R500: by 12% at R500 and by 30% at 2.7 R500.

Emulator facts for d-02. CGD and CTP come out already scaled: rho_gas/rho_crit and T/T500 on 19 log bins of r/R500, spanning 0.015 to 2.74. Halo mass is not an input. args.claim: Redshift shift compared with kinetic-AGN spread. Approximation: dln n/dln r is held at the fiducial d-01 value (-2.54 at z=0, -2.74 at z=0.4987) for both variants, and M_HSE ∝ t(s_n+s_T). On that basis, the z=0 to 0.4987 change in ln t(R500) is -0.144 for AGN-min and -0.132 for AGN-max. The fiducial value from d-01 is -0.134. This is about twice the AGN spread in ln t at fixed z (0.060 at z=0, 0.071 at z=0.4987), so the redshift drop in scaled temperature is robust to kinetic-AGN feedback. For M_HSE,500c the picture is different. The shape-only redshift shift is -9.0% (AGN-min) or -5.6% (AGN-max) in ln M, against the fiducial -9.2%. The AGN-max minus AGN-min difference at fixed z is +4.6% at z=0 and +8.1% at z=0.4987. These are of the same size, so the M_HSE redshift shift cannot be cleanly separated from kinetic-feedback uncertainty. The GP y_std on t(R500) is about 1% at z=0 and 2-3% at z=0.4987, so the AGN spread in t is about 4 sigma at z=0 and about 2 sigma at z=0.4987.

args.claim: Fiducial R500 inputs recomputed from the four fiducial CSVs, using finite differences between the 0.866 and 1.155 R500 bins (dln x = 0.2878). At z=0: s_rho = -2.545, s_T = -0.583, sum = -3.128, t(R500) = 0.5916 (geometric mean), giving M_th/M500 = (t/2)|sum| = 0.925. At z=0.4987: s_rho = -2.738, s_T = -0.505, sum = -3.243, t = 0.5181, giving M_th/M500 = 0.840. In the FLAMINGO convention, uncorrected b_HSE = (M_HSE - M500)/M500 = -0.075 (z=0) and -0.160 (z=0.4987). The shape-only shift is -9.2%. This reproduces f-004 and f-005.
args.note: I did the arithmetic by hand from the CSV values that the tools returned. It assumes kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), which the tool does not confirm.

args.claim: Nelson+14 f_nth correction at R500, using A=0.452, B=0.841, gamma=1.628 and P_tot = P_th/(1-f). The formula is M_tot/M500 = (t/2)/(1-f) * [-(s_n+s_T) + dln(1-f)/dln r], with dln(1-f)/dln r = -gamma*u*e^-u/(1+e^-u) and u = (r/R200m/B)^gamma. For the radius conversion I assumed an NFW profile with c200c=4 and Omega_m=0.3, which gives R500c = 0.652 R200c. R200m is 1.69 R200c at z=0 (Omega_m(z)=0.30) and 1.265 R200c at z=0.4987 (Omega_m(z)=0.59), so R200m/R500c = 2.60 and 1.94. At z=0: R500 = 0.385 R200m, f_nth = 0.207 and dln(1-f)/dln r = -0.196, so M_tot/M500 = 0.3728 * 2.932 = 1.093. At z=0.4987: R500 = 0.515 R200m, f_nth = 0.260 and dln(1-f)/dln r = -0.285, so M_tot/M500 = 0.3500 * 2.958 = 1.035. The corrected b_HSE is +0.09 (z=0) and +0.035 (z=0.4987), which overcorrects. The correction factor M_tot/M_th is 1.18 at z=0 and 1.23 at z=0.4987, and the corrected redshift shift is -5.3% instead of -9.2%. If R200m/R500c is held at 2.60 at both redshifts, the shift stays at -9.2%. So the redshift dependence of the correction comes entirely from the assumed evolution of R200m/R500c.
args.note: These are hand calculations. The NFW concentration, Omega_m and T500 convention are all assumptions. The parameter quote is in references.bib (arxiv14044636). At R500, f_nth of about 21-26% is well above the X-COP median of about 6% given in f-002, and that number is not backed by a bib quote.

args.claim: Benchmark comparison. The redshift trend of the thermal HSE mass is set by profile shape: the scaled T at R500 drops 12.4%, partly offset by a 3.7% steepening of the slope sum. This matches the sign of FLAMINGO's quoted cluster trend, where hydrostatic masses decrease with redshift at fixed true mass. The Nelson f_nth correction changes the size of the trend only through the assumed R200m/R500c evolution, reducing it from -9.2% to -5.3%. Feedback cannot yet be ranked because d-06 is pending. On SPT, the emulator cools by 12% at R500 and 30% at 2.7 R500 between z=0 and 0.5, while SPT reports about 40% cooler scaled temperatures for 0.6<z<1.2 than for 0.3<z<0.6. The redshift bins do not overlap, so this is qualitative only. No X-COP T/T500 or scaled-density values were quoted, so no profile comparison with X-COP was made.
args.note: Bib quotes support the FLAMINGO z-trend, the FLAMINGO fit sensitivity, the SPT 40% cooling and the Nelson parameters. The FLAMINGO -0.1/-0.2, X-COP 6%/1-b=0.85 and Planck B~0.6/0.8 numbers come from abstracts (f-002) and have no verbatim quotes in references.bib.

args.claim: The fiducial R500 numbers now trace to tool output (tc-...-94 to -97, all bins shown). I differenced ln y between the r/R500 = 0.866 and 1.155 bins, whose geometric midpoint is 1.000, with spacing dln r = 0.2878, and took t(R500) as the geometric mean of the two bins. At z=0: dln rho/dln r = -2.545, dln T/dln r = -0.583, t = 0.592 and M_HSE,500c/M500 = 0.925, so b_HSE = (M_HSE - M500)/M500 = -0.075. At z=0.4987: -2.738, -0.505, t = 0.518, M_HSE/M500 = 0.840 and b_HSE = -0.160. The mass assumes kT500 = G mu m_p M500/(2 R500), so the absolute values depend on the T500 convention.

Error bracket on the fiducial numbers, using the GP y_std. Upper bound (adjacent bins independent, density and temperature independent): z=0 slopes -2.545+-0.155 and -0.583+-0.055, M_HSE/M500 = 0.925+-0.049; z=0.4987 slopes -2.738+-0.100 and -0.505+-0.135, M_HSE/M500 = 0.840+-0.047. Lower bound (adjacent bins fully correlated): slope errors 0.007/0.002 at z=0 and 0.022/0.025 at z=0.4987; M_HSE/M500 = 0.925+-0.010 and 0.840+-0.018. The shape-only shift M_HSE,500c(z=0.4987)/M_HSE,500c(z=0) - 1 = -9.2%. Its error is +-7.0% (1.3 sigma) for independent bins and +-2.1% (4.3 sigma) for fully correlated bins. f-008's +-0.3 in T500 units (+-0.15 M500) overstates the error: the independent-bin error is +-0.10 in T500 units (+-0.05 M500).
args.note: Linear propagation was done by hand; no Monte Carlo was possible. The two redshifts are treated as independent GP predictions. The real GP covariance between bins is unknown, so the true significance lies between 1.3 and 4.3 sigma.
